planting.note: Plant corms in fall into well-drained soil on a sunny slope that stays dry through summer dormancy.

directions: A striking northern California and southern Oregon native corm bearing umbels of pendant, tubular red flowers tipped with green or pale yellow, resembling a cluster of firecrackers atop a tall wiry stem in late spring. Found naturally on rocky slopes and in open woodland, it demands fast drainage and a dry summer rest to persist, often rotting if kept irrigated through its dormant season. A long-standing favorite of specialty California-native bulb growers and the Pacific Bulb Society for its vivid, hummingbird-pollinated flowers.
